tra_loi.Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies over the tower on the hillside (frames 40-41), and the soldiers there wear dark coats. Nothing on screen names the nation, so this rests on the flag.
tra_loi.Q2: A siege. The caption 'The Great Siege' appears at frame 23 (21 Jun 1779), followed by large camps of white tents and a line of soldiers and cattle on the land side, with ships blockading the bay. The pictures don't say who is besieging.
tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures don't show hunger directly. The town is cut off by the camps on land and the ships in the bay, and there is a scene of soldiers with barrels or crates (frames 48-50), but nothing shows people starving or food running short.
tra_loi.Q4: A fleet of ships sailing in from the sea (frame 47, 18 Jan 1780), and later ships near the port (frames 51-52). The pictures don't show clearly whether they are relief ships or what they bring. The soldiers unloading barrels at the wall (frames 48-49) suggest supplies were delivered.

tra_loi.Q1: Britain. A Union Jack flies on the tower of the fortified town in frames 40-41 (Jan 1780), and the town is under siege during 1779-1781.
tra_loi.Q2: '1779 — The Great Siege', shown by the caption in frame 23. Rows of tents and a line of earthworks or trenches grow on the land side of the Rock (frames 27-33), and ships gather in the bay (34-39).
tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show hunger or starvation directly. The likely cause is the siege: the land is blockaded by the camps and trenches, and ships ring the bay. No text or image mentions food shortage.
tra_loi.Q4: Ships. A fleet of sailing ships arrives in the bay on 18 Jan 1780 (frame 47), and barrels or supplies are then unloaded and carried into the fortress (frames 48-50). The pictures do not name the fleet or say who sent it.

tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show hunger directly. A ship arrives in frames 36-38 and ships are blockading in 43-47, which hints that supplies are cut off. Nothing shows starving people or empty stores.
